page: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-4 is an instance within the memory-optimized server family, configured on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs and 62.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration is structured to handle applications where memory footprint requirements exceed typical compute demands.

The server includes no integrated local storage and contains no discrete hardware GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for system disks and persistent data volumes. It is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware setup avoids over-allocating compute cores to access higher memory capacities, offering resource balance for applications constrained by working dataset sizes.

Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-4 is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require low-to-moderate thread concurrency, including in-memory caching systems, transactional databases with moderate query parallelization, and data preparation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 62.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory-to-core density of 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes with no integrated local storage and no GPU hardware accelerators, requiring attached network storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Furthermore, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The platform architecture targets scenarios where dataset residency in memory takes priority over high vCPU counts. By offering a high ratio of memory per core, this instance profile provides resource efficiency for memory-constrained workloads without forcing overprovisioning of compute cores. Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-4 is engineered for memory-bound applications such as in-memory databases, memory caching servers, data processing tasks, and database instances managing medium working sets.
